title: Tokyo Revengers: War of the Three Titans Arc (Season 4) Reveals Third Trailer, Anime Expo 2026 Appearance
content:
Tokyo Revengers: War of the Three Titans Arc (Season 4) sequel anime revealed a new trailer, along with an October 2 premiere date. The anime previously revealed the voice cast for the founding members of Black Dragon , as well as South Terano. The anime will stream exclusively on Disney+ worldwide.

Special appearances were also confirmed for Anime Expo 2026 in Los Angeles and AnimagiC 2026 in Germany. Anime Expo 2026 will host a Tokyo Revengers special cast panel on July 4 featuring Yuki Shin (Takemichi), Yuu Hayashi (Mikey), and Masaya Fukunishi (Draken). Meanwhile, Chifuyu Matsuno voice actor Sho Karino will appear at AnimagiC 2026 in Mannheim, Germany, on August 1.

The anime was announced in July 2024 with a teaser visual featuring Takemichi Inagaki and Manjiro Sano (Mikey). It will continue after the Tenjiku Arc . A teaser visual was shown at AnimeJapan in March. Maki Kodaira is taking over as director from Koichi Hatsumi, who directed the first three seasons.

You can watch the new trailer below.

The listed staff for the new Tokyo Revengers anime includes:

• Director: Maki Kodaira

• Series Composition: Yasuyuki Muto

• Character Design: Kenichi Ohnuki / Keiko Ota / Airi Tsuyuki / Kae Takakura

• Bike & Prop Design: Hideki Fukushima / Yoshitomo Hara

• Art Director: Rumi Matsumoto

• Art Settings: Yuho Taniuchi

• Color Design: Kunio Tsujita

• Director of Photography: 家高浩司

• Sound Director: Satoki Iida

• Music: Hiroaki Tsutsumi

• Animation Production: LIDENFILMS

You can also see the full cast for the anime:

• Yuki Shin as Takemichi Hanagaki

• Azumi Waki as Hinata Tachibana (Hina)

• Ryota Osaka as Naoto Tachibana

• Yuu Hayashi as Manjiro Sano (Mikey)

• Masaya Fukunishi as Ken Ryuguji (Draken)

• Sho Karino as Chifuyu Matsuno

• Yoshitsugu Matsuoka as Takashi Mitsuya

• Tasuku Hatanaka as Hakkai Shiba

• Masaaki Mizunaka as Keisuke Baji

• Yukihiro Nozuyama as Ryohei Hayashi (Peh-yan)

• Kengo Kawanishi as Nahoya Kawata (Smiley)

• Daisuke Ono as Yasuhiro Muto (Mucho)

• Takuma Terashima as Atsushi Sendo (Akkun)

• Yuya Hirose as Takuya Yamamoto

• Shunsuke Takeuchi as Makoto Suzuki

• Shota Hayama as Kazushi Yamagishi

• Yumi Uchiyama as Emma Sano

• Showtaro Morikubo as Tetta Kisaki

• Takuya Eguchi as Shuji Hanma

• Junya Enoki as Seishu Inui

• Natsuki Hanae as Kokonoi Hajime

• Tomokazu Sugita as Taiju Shiba

• Nobunaga Shimazaki as Izana Kurokawa

• Seiichiro Yamashita as Kakucho

• Tetsu Inada as Kanji Mochizuki

• Koki Uchiyama as Shion Madarame

• Daisuke Namikawa as Ran Haitani

• Hiro Shimono as Rindo Haitani

About Tokyo Revengers

The first season of the anime aired from April 11 to September 19, 2021. Most of the cast reprised their roles in the second season, which premiered in January 2023 and had Masaya Fukunishi replacing Tatsuhisa Suzuki (the first season was also edited to reflect the changes). The third season , covering the Tenjiku Arc , premiered in October 2023 and is available worldwide exclusively on Disney+ (excluding mainland China).

The Tokyo Revengers anime is based on the manga by Ken Wakui. The manga was serialized in the Weekly Shonen Magazine from March 2017 to November 2022, officially ending on November 16 that year. Kodansha is publishing it in English, and they describe the story: Watching the news, Takemichi Hanagaki learns that his girlfriend from way back in middle school, Hinata Tachibana, has died. The only girlfriend he ever had was just killed by a villainous group known as the Tokyo Manji Gang. He lives in a crappy apartment with thin walls, and his six-years-younger boss treats him like an idiot. Plus, he’s a complete and total virgin … At the height of his rock-bottom life, he suddenly time-leaps twelve years back to his middle school days!! To save Hinata, and change the life he spent running away, hopeless part-timer Takemichi must aim for the top of Kanto’s most sinister delinquent gang!!
author: Anime Corner

title: Kyoto Animation's Sparks of Tomorrow Anime Reveals New Visual and Broadcast Trailer
content:
Sparks of Tomorrow anime by Kyoto Animation revealed a new key visual and trailer ahead of its July 5, 2026 premiere. The anime by Kyoto Animation will stream exclusively on Netflix . Minoru Ota is directing the TV anime, with Tatsuhiko Urahata in charge of the script. Yuma Uchida voices Kihachi Sakamoto, with Sora Amamiya as Inako Momokawa. The first trailer was revealed in October 2025.

You can see the new visual below.

The introduction is described:

A Tale of Adventure for Boys and Girls Who Dreamed of the Age of Electricity in a World Shrouded in Smoke! ──This was a little while ago. Kyoto in the early 20th century, having evolved differently from the history we know today. In a world where only steam engines had advanced, the city was shrouded in smoke. A boy who lost his brother, with whom he had dreamed of the “Age of Electricity,” and now lives with deep suspicion. A girl who keeps her dreams for the future and her regrets for her deceased mother hidden in her heart, now living a devout life. The boy and girl meet while seeking the secret of the “20th Century Electrical Catalog,” which depicted their dreams. Surpass who you are now and break through the dreams you once had! This is the story of .

Main staff:

• Director: Minoru Ota

• Series Composition: Tatsuhiko Urahata

• Character Design / Chief Animation Director: Kohei Okamura

• Worldview Setting: Takaaki Suzuki

• Music: Hitomi Koto

• Animation Studio: Kyoto Animation

Four new cast additions were also announced.

• Hiroshi Yanaka as Jinemon Momokawa

• Mayumi Asano as Naeko Momokawa

• Daichi Endo as Bunshichi Yagura

• Ayahi Takagaki as Tome / Inari

You can watch the new trailer below.

title: Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club Final Chapter Movie Unveils Key Visual
content:
Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club Final Chapter Part 3 movie, set to begin this winter , has unveiled its key visual featuring the never before seen dance costumes of Karin Asaka and Kasumi Nakasu. The announcement was made after Nijigasaki’s 8th live concert, “Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club 8th Live! TOKIMEKI Express,” held on Sunday.

A trailer for the new visual was also released:

The first part of the trilogy premiered in Japan on September 6, 2024, while the second part was released on November 7, 2025. The voice cast consists of:

• Hinaki Yano as Yu Takasaki

• Aguri Onishi as Ayumu Uehara

• Akari Kito as Kanata Konoe

• Chiemi Tanaka as Rina Tennoji

• Kaori Maeda as Shizuku Osaka

• Maria Sashide as Emma Verde

• Mayu Sagara as Kasumi Nakasu

• Miyu Kubota as Karin Asaka

• Natsumi Murakami as Ai Miyashita

• Coco Hayashi as Setsuna Yuki

• Moeka Koizumi as Shioriko Mifune

• Akina Homoto as Lanzhu Zhong

• Shu Uchida as Mia Taylor

Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club is a spin-off project of Love Live! idol franchise. The first season began broadcasting in October 2020 while the second aired in April 2022. An OVA premiered in June 2023. Studio Sunrise was in charge of all the production of the Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club anime.

Crunchyroll is streaming the first and second seasons of Love Live Nijigasaki School Idol Club anime and describes it as: Nijigasaki High School is known for their diverse subjects and the freedom they give to students. Second-year student Yu Takasaki has been turned on to the charms of school idols, so she knocks on the door of the School Idol Club with her friend, Ayumu Uehara. Sometimes friends, sometimes rivals, the members of this club each contribute their own thoughts and motivations to the group.
author: Anime Corner

title: 'Oni no Hanayome' Unveils Additional Staff, Theme Songs, First Promo
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Kureha 's Oni no Hanayome ( The Ogre's Bride ) novel unveiled additional staff, a key visual (pictured), the theme songs, and first promotional video on Sunday. The anime series is scheduled to premiere on July 5 at 12:30 a.m. on Tokyo MX, BS11, Gunma TV, and Tochigi TV, followed by CBC TV, Yomiuri TV, and other stations.

Staff Art Director, Art Setting: MAI MAI ( Boku ga Aishita Subete no Kimi e ) Color Design: Akiko Shibata ( Code Geass: Fukkatsu no Lelouch ) Director of Photography: Tomoyoshi Ishizuka ( Haite Kudasai, Takamine-san ) Editing: Junichi Itou ( Arifureta Shokugyou de Sekai Saikyou ) Sound Director: Kazuhiro Wakabayashi ( Bungou Stray Dogs ) Sound Production: Rakuonsha

Music group ClariS ( Lycoris Recoil ) is performing the opening theme "Hikoto." Japanese actor Ikusaburo Yamazaki ( Tasogare Out Focus opening theme) is performing the ending theme "Shinboshi." Both theme songs are previewed in the promotional video below.

Kazuhito Oomiya ( Chou Shounen Tanteidan Neo ) is directing the anime at Colored Pencil Animation Japan , with Yumi Kamakura ( Working!!! director ) handling the series composition. Hikari Tanaka ( Obey Me! ) is in charge of the main character design, while Hiroko Shigekuni ( Fruits Basket: Prelude chief animation director) serves as character designer. Masaru Yokoyama ( Tomo-chan wa Onnanoko! ) is composing the music.

Kureha originally began penning the fantasy romance novel on the Novema! website in 2019. Starts Shuppan began publishing the novel under its Starts Shuppan Bunko imprint with illustrations by Yuu Shiratani in October 2020 and released the ninth volume in May 2024.

Jun Togashi began drawing a manga adaptation on the Star Shuppan's noicomi web magazine in December 2021. Star Shuppan published the ninth volume on March 27.

NTT Solmare began publishing the manga in English on its Manga Plaza platform in March 2025.

title: The Ogre's Bride Anime's New Video Unveils Theme Songs, More Staff, July 4 Debut
content:
The staff for the television anime of Kureha 's The Ogre's Bride ( Oni no Hanayome ) light novel series presented the anime's full promotional video and a new key visual on Sunday. The video announces and previews the anime's theme songs, and it also announces additional staff members and July 4 premiere for the anime.

The ClariS trio are performing the anime's opening theme song "Hitokoto" (A Word). The song will be available on digital music services on July 5 at midnight (July 4 at 11:00 a.m. EDT). The " ClariS 15th Thanks Tour ~Ichige Tōsai~" (A Summer Lantern Festival) will add another concert under the additional subtitle "Musubi-yo" (Final Night) in Tokyo on September 18.

Actor and singer Ikusaburō Yamazaki is performing the ending theme song "Shinboshi."

The anime's newly announced staff members are:

• Art Director, Art Setting: Mai Mai

• Color Key Artist: Akiko Shibata

• Compositing Director of Photography: Tomoyoshi Ishizuka

• Editing: Junichi Itou

• Sound Director: Kazuhiro Wakabayashi

• Sound Production: Rakuonsha

The anime will premiere in Japan on the Tokyo MX , BS11 , Gunma TV , and Tochigi TV channels, as well as on the d Anime Store , ABEMA , U-NEXT , and Anime Hōdai streaming services, on July 4 at 24:30 (effectively, July 5 at 12:30 a.m.) It will then play on nine more channels throughout Japan and other streaming platforms.

The novel series is set in a Japan where humans and demons co-exist peacefully. Yuzu is an ordinary high school girl, who lives in the shadow of her older sister who is the bride of a demon. One day, she has a life-changing encounter with a beautiful ogre who claims her as his bride.

The cast includes:

• Saori Hayami as Yuzu Shinonome

• Yūichirō Umehara as Reiya Kiryuin

• Manaka Iwami as Karin Shinonome

• Ryōta Ōsaka as Yōta Kogetsu

• Sayaka Senbongi as Tōko

• Natsuki Hanae as Tōkichi Nekota

• Taito Ban as Takamichi Araki

• Nobunaga Shimazaki as Ouga Kiyama

• Aya Endō as Sakurako Kiyama

• Momoka Terasawa as Sou

• Miyu Kobashi as Ao

Kazuhito Ōmiya is directing the anime at Colored Pencil Animation Japan . Yumi Kamakura is in charge of the series scripts. Hikari Tanaka is drawing the main character designs, and Hiroko Shigekuni is also credited for character designs. Masaru Yokoyama is composing the music.

Kureha began the light novel series on Starts Publishing 's Novema! platform in 2019. The series won the grand prize at the First Novema! Character Short Story Contest. Starts published the ninth volume in May 2024. Yū Shiroya illustrates the series.

Jun Togashi launched the manga adaptation in Starts Publishing 's Noicomi magazine in December 2021. The manga adaptation won Noicomi's annual comic ranking in the girl comics category in 2022 and 2023. Starts shipped the ninth compiled book volume on March 27. MangaPlaza is releasing the manga in English.

The light novel series and its manga adaptation collectively have over 5.8 million copies in circulation.

The novel series also inspired a live-action film that opened on March 27. The film sold 146,000 tickets for 202,395,960 yen (about US$1.27 million) in its opening three days.

title: Sakanaction's 'Kaiju' Song Wins Song of the Year at Music Awards Japan 2026
content:
The major award winners are:

• Artist of the Year Mrs. Green Apple

• Song of the Year "Kaiju" by sakanaction (from Orb: On the Movements of the Earth)

• New Artist of the Year HANA

• Album of the Year Prema by Kaze Fujii

• Best Global Hit from Japan "HYPNOTIZE" by XG

• Best Song Asia "Golden" by HUNTR/X (from KPop Demon Hunters)

Other notable award winners include:

• Best J-POP Song "IRIS OUT" by Kenshi Yonezu (from Chainsaw Man – The Movie: Reze Arc)

• Best J-POP Artist Mrs. Green Apple

• Best Rock Song "Kaiju" by sakanaction

• Best Rock Band/Solo Artist sakanaction

• Best Hip Hop/Rap Song "doppelgänger" by Creepy Nuts (from the live-action Under Ninja film)

• Best Hip Hop/Rap Artist Creepy Nuts

• Best Anime Song "Kaiju" by sakanaction

• Best Original Score for Animation "Lazarus" soundtrack by Kamasi Washington, Bonobo, Floating Points

• Best Vocaloid Culture Song Award "A Spoonful of SPELL" by r-906

• Best Girls Idol Culture Artist FRUITS ZIPPER

• Special Award: Fandom Best Fandom Artist powered by LINE MUSIC & Yahoo! Japan Search Mrs. Green Apple

The Grand Ceremony featured performances by Mrs. Green Apple , M!LK, FRUITS ZIPPER , Fujii, sakanaction , LiSA , Yonezu, and more.

Yonezu's "IRIS OUT" also won Best Japanese Song in Asia, Best Japanese Song in Europe, Best Japanese Song in North America, and Best Japanese Song in Latin America.

sakanaction 's "Kaiju" also won Best Music Video. Ado won the award for Largest Live Audience (International).

Music Awards Japan also presented a special “MAJ Timeless Echo” award to Tatsuro Yamashita ( Summer Wars , Mirai ). The award was in "recognition for the artist who [has] long contributed to and excelled in the Japanese music industry."

The full list of the more than 70 award winners is available on the Music Awards Japan's website .

Mrs. Green Apple also won Artist of the Year at the inaugural awards last year, and "Bling-Bang-Bang-Born" by Creepy Nuts won Song of the Year. YOASOBI 's "Idol" (from Oshi no Ko ) won Best Anime Song last year.

The Music Awards Japan is intended to honor the best musicians in Japan as well as international artists from all over Asia, and have over 70 total award categories, including honors for "Vocaloid culture," anime, and "idol culture." More than 5,000 music industry professionals from Japan and abroad voted for the winners.

The CEIPA is a collaboration amongst five music industry bodies from Japan.

title: Sparks of Tomorrow Anime Reveals New Promo Video, 5 More Cast Members
content:
The staff for the television anime of Hiro Yūki 's Sparks of Tomorrow ( 20 Seiki Denki Mokuroku ) novel revealed a pre-broadcast promotional video on Sunday.

The staff also revealed a new visual and more cast.

The new cast includes:

Hiroshi Yanaka as Jinemon Momokawa, Inako's father

Mayumi Asano as Naeko Momokawa, Inako's mother

Daichi Endō as Bunshichi Yagura, Yajiro's father and Kihachi's uncle

Ayahi Takagaki as Tome, a maid working for the Momokawa family

Ayahi Takagaki as Inari, an ermine that is fond of Inako

The anime will debut on July 5 and will air on Sundays at 11:00 p.m. on Tokyo MX and on 11:30 on BS11 . The series will also air on ABC TV and TV Aichi . The anime will exclusively stream worldwide on Netflix on Sundays starting on July 5 at 11:00 p.m. JST.

The anime will have a world premiere tour with stops in Japan, the U.K., Thailand, and North America. The North American premiere will be at Anime Expo on July 3.

The anime will star:

• Yūma Uchida as Kihachi Sakamoto

• Sora Amamiya as Inako Momokawa

• Kōki Uchiyama as Yosuke Mizoe

• Daisuke Ono as Seiroku Sakamoto

• Shunsuke Takeuchi as Kengo Kuga

• Minako Kotobuki as Noriko Momokawa

• Yō Taichi as Suzu Harashima

• Natsumi Kawaida as Kate Okura

• Kazuki Ura as Yajiro Yagura

• Daisuke Hirakawa as Izo Masubuchi

Minoru Ōta (key animator for Love, Chunibyo & Other Delusions! , Liz and the Blue Bird ; episode director for CITY The Animation , Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid S ) is directing the anime as his first directorial project. Tatsuhiko Urahata ( Haganai , Hi Score Girl , Saki Episode of Side A ) is overseeing the series scripts. Kohei Okamura ( Free! The Final Stroke chief animation director, Sound! Euphonium key animator) is the chief animation director and character designer. Takaaki Suzuki ( Violet Evergarden , Strike Witches ) is in charge of the worldview setting, and Hitomi Kotō is composing the music.

Luna Goami performs the opening the song "Eureka Evrika," and Ginger Root performs the ending theme song "Soarin'."

Kyoto Animation had announced the anime adaptation in July 2018.

The novel won an honorable mention in the full-length novel category at the 8th Kyoto Animation Awards in May 2017. The entry was the only one to win any of the awards available that year. Kyoto Animation 's KA Esuma Bunko label published the novel in August 2018. Kazumi Ikeda illustrated the novel, and Momoka Nagatani is credited with art and background.

The novel takes place in the summer of 1907, the 40th year of the Meiji era. 15-year-old Inako Momokawa lives in the Fushimi area of Kyoto, and is the second daughter of a sake brewer. Nothing she does ever comes out right, and she receives a scolding from her father every day. Her only relief is the trust she places in her prayers to the gods. One day while at Fushimi Inari shrine, she meets a freewheeling young man named Kihachi Sakamoto. He rejects the gods, and boasts of the incoming age of electricity.

The topic of marriage suddenly comes up in Inako's household. Her father is one-sidedly making all the decisions for her, and Inako is about to give up hope. It is then that Kihachi draws out Inako's true feelings of wanting to run away from her family. The only way to stop her marriage is to find an unusual book called the "Electrical Catalog." The book is a prediction book about electricity that Kihachi wrote when he was a child, but his older brother Seiroku took the book, and its current whereabouts are unknown. Inako and Kihachi together go in search of the book across Kyoto and Shiga prefectures.

title: 'Nijusseiki Denki Mokuroku: Eureka Evrika' Unveils Additional Cast, Third Promo
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Hiro Yuuki 's Nijusseiki Denki Mokuroku ( 20th Century Electricity Catalog ) light novel unveiled additional cast, a third key visual (pictured), and the third promotional video on Sunday. The anime series is scheduled to premiere on July 5 at 11:00 p.m. on Tokyo MX and exclusively worldwide on Netflix, followed by BS11, ABC TV, and TV Aichi.

Cast Jinemon Momokawa: Hiroshi Yanaka ( Naruto ) Naeko Momokawa: Mayumi Asano ( Fuguushoku "Kanteishi" ga Jitsu wa Saikyou Datta ) Bunshichi Yagura: Daichi Endou ( Boku no Hero Academia 3rd Season ) Tome : Ayahi Takagaki ( Akatsuki no Yona )

Minoru Oota ( Kobayashi-san Chi no Maid Dragon S episode director) is helming the anime at Kyoto Animation , with Tatsuhiko Urahata ( Ookami to Koushinryou: Merchant Meets the Wise Wolf ) handling the series composition. Kouhei Okamura ( Free! Movie: The Final Stroke ) is designing the characters and serving as chief animation director, while Takaaki Suzuki ( Violet Evergarden ) is in charge of world design. Hitomi Koto is composing the music.

The light novel won Honorable Mention at the 8th Kyoto Animation Award in 2017. Yuuki published the title under Kyoto Animation KA Esuma Bunko label with illustrations by Kazumi Ikeda ( Hibike! Euphonium 3 character design) in August 2018.

title: Naoki Urasawa to Launch New Manga 'Saigo no Manga Kyoushitsu' in August 2026
content:
Veteran manga creator Naoki Urasawa will begin a new manga titled Saigo no Manga Kyoushitsu ( The Final Manga Classroom ) in the September issue of Big Comic Original Zoukan on August 12. The announcement was made in the magazine's July issue on Friday.

The magazine preview suggests that the new series will touch on themes related to artificial intelligence and creativity. It notes that although modern society has become increasingly convenient, there are values and experiences from earlier times that were cultivated through patience and craftsmanship, encouraging readers to reexamine what may have been lost amid technological progress.

Urasawa resumed serializing Asadora! on March 23 after the manga had been on hiatus since July 2025. The series originally launched in Weekly Big Comic Spirits in October 2018.

Urasawa made his manga debut in 1981 and has established himself as one of Japan's most acclaimed creators. His major works include Monster , Master Keaton , Yawara! , 20th Century Boys , 21st Century Boys , Pluto ( Pluto: Urasawa x Tezuka ), and Billy Bat .

Several of his manga have received anime adaptations over the years. Yawara! was adapted into a television anime in 1989, followed by Master Keaton in 1998. Monster received a 74-episode television anime adaptation in 2004.

Pluto , Urasawa's reinterpretation of Osamu Tezuka 's Chikyuu Saidai no Robot ( The Greatest Robot on Earth ) arc from Tetsuwan Atom ( Astro Boy ), streamed on Netflix in October 2023. 20th Century Boys inspired a live-action film trilogy between 2008 and 2009.

title: Aoteru Makes His Move in NIPPON SANGOKU Episode 11 Preview
content:
NIPPON SANGOKU revealed the preview images and synopsis for Episode 11, which is set to premiere on Sunday, June 14. Studio Kafka is in charge of the animation. The anime is co-produced with Amazon MGM Studios and is currently streaming weekly on Prime Video.

You can see the preview trailer and synopsis below.

Aoteru finally reunites with Taira, but Taira’s eyes are fixed on something else entirely. “I wish to receive from His Majesty an imperial decree ordering our withdrawal.” Aoteru reveals the true intent behind his proposal to withdraw, yet Taira remains opposed. In the end, the decision is left to the Emperor.

Also check out some more preview images for the upcoming episode:

The voice cast for the anime includes:

• Kensho Ono as Aoteru Misumi

• Seto Asami as Saki Higashimachi

• Takashi Nagasako as Denki Taira

• Megumi Han as Narrator

The staff includes:

• Original Story: “NIPPON SANGOKU” by Ikka Matsuki, published by Shogakukan

• Director: Kazuaki Terasawa

• Character Design/Chief Animation Director: Takahiko Abiru

• Animation Studio: STUDIO KAFKA (The Ancient Magus’ Bride)

• Production: NIPPON SANGOKU Partners

NIPPON SANGOKU (meaning “Japan: Three Kingdoms”) is a manga series by Ikka Matsuki, who serves as both writer and artist. The series started publication in November 2021 through Shogakukan’s Ura Sunday platform and the MangaONE app. The official introduction:

In a near-future Japan where civilization has regressed due to nuclear war, natural disasters, and corrupt governance. The nation fractures into three, plunging into a new Three Kingdoms era as each vies for supremacy. Aoteru Misumi, once an obscure local bureaucrat, sets his sights on the reunification of Japan. Armed with vast knowledge and exceptional eloquence, he steadily rises. The legend of the man later known as the prodigious strategist begins now.
author: Anime Corner
